title: Pollis App manifest (pollis-app.json)
description: What a Pollis App asks for. An admin can narrow it when approving the App, never widen it; the runtime enforces the manifest intersected with the admin's grants. Pairs with the WIT package pollis:app@0.1.0.

name.description: Lowercase letters, digits and '-', 1 to 64 characters.

version.description: The App's own version, shown to admins.

triggers.description: What can wake the App. Each maps to one exported handler.

channels.description: "#name" for one channel by name, or "*" for whichever channels the admin grants.

history.description: Days of history query-messages may reach back. 0: none.

events.description: Message event kinds the App may see.

actions.description: What the App may do in the group. There are no moderation actions.

quota.description: Bytes of keys plus values in the installation's sealed key-value state. 0: no state.

schedules.description: When the `schedule` trigger fires; required with it and refused without it. Each fires at every Unix time k * every + offset (UTC seconds).

offset.description: Seconds after each period boundary; less than every.

egress.description: Exact host names the App may reach over HTTPS. No wildcards, IP literals, ports or schemes. Empty: the App cannot send data outside the group.

commands.description: Slash commands members can pick in the composer (#2018). A command is an ordinary message starting with /name; the runtime hands it to on-command only if it is declared here and the App takes the commands trigger. With request: true it is delivered to the bot as a sealed request (on-request) and never posted in the channel. Names are unique.

name.description: Typed after the slash. Lowercase letters, digits, '-' and '_', starting with a letter, 1 to 32 characters.

description.description: One line shown beside the name in the composer.

arg_hint.description: What to type after the name, shown greyed ("<title>"). Leave it out for a command without arguments.

request.description: Deliver as a sealed request to the bot (on-request; needs the requests trigger) instead of posting in the channel (on-command; needs the commands trigger).
